data.summary: Prioritized implementation plan for the first release of the customer support portal: sign-in, then account recovery, then support request creation, then request status reading, with a release check gating on keyboard navigation and screen-reader support. Two stages remain blocked: account recovery acceptance criteria and the accessibility verification method.
claims: Scope is a first release of a customer support portal for existing customers; implementation has not started (context).
Required capabilities per the brief: sign in, recover an account, open a support request, read request status.
Accessibility is release-blocking: the first release must work with keyboard navigation and screen readers (brief).
Priority 1 is sign-in, since recovery and request flows depend on an authenticated identity.
Priority 2 is account recovery, blocked until its acceptance criteria are defined (outstanding).
Priority 3 is opening a support request; Priority 4 is reading request status, which depends on request creation.
Priority 5 is a release check covering keyboard navigation and screen-reader support across all four flows.
The accessibility verification method is undefined (outstanding), so the release check cannot yet be stated as a pass/fail gate.
New-customer registration is out of scope; brief and context cover existing customers only.
unresolved: Account recovery acceptance criteria are undefined, so that work item cannot be sized or accepted.
Accessibility verification method is undefined: tooling, assistive-technology matrix, and pass threshold are unspecified.
No stated recovery channel (email, phone, support-agent assisted) or identity-proofing bar for recovery.
No stated support-request fields, status values, or notification behavior for status reading.
No timeline, team capacity, or platform/browser targets given, so priority order is dependency-based rather than schedule-based.

data.summary: Prioritized plan for the first release of the customer support portal, covering existing customers only: (1) sign-in, (2) account recovery, (3) open a support request, (4) read request status, (5) a release-gating accessibility check for keyboard navigation and screen readers across all four flows. Account recovery and the accessibility verification method remain undefined and block full acceptance of priorities 2 and 5.
claims: Scope is the first release of a customer support portal for existing customers; implementation has not started (context).
Required capabilities per the brief: sign in, recover an account, open a support request, read request status.
The brief makes keyboard navigation and screen-reader support release-blocking for the first release.
Priority 1: sign-in, because account recovery, request creation, and status reading all require an authenticated identity.
Priority 2: account recovery, sequenced after sign-in but held at not-ready status because its acceptance criteria are undefined (outstanding).
Priority 3: open a support request, sequenced after sign-in since request creation needs an authenticated customer.
Priority 4: read request status, sequenced after request creation since a request must exist before its status can be read.
Priority 5: a release check verifying keyboard navigation and screen-reader support across sign-in, recovery, request creation, and status reading.
The release check in Priority 5 cannot be stated as a pass/fail gate yet because the accessibility verification method is undefined (outstanding).
New-customer registration is explicitly out of scope; both the brief and context describe existing customers only.
This plan is a repaired candidate produced after a prior version was rejected; no new acceptance criteria were supplied with the rejection, so the same two stages remain blocked.
unresolved: Account recovery acceptance criteria are undefined, so Priority 2 cannot be sized, scheduled, or marked accepted.
Accessibility verification method is undefined: no stated tooling, assistive-technology test matrix, or pass/fail threshold for Priority 5.
No recovery channel (email, phone, agent-assisted) or identity-proofing bar is specified for account recovery.
No support-request fields, status values, or notification behavior are specified for request creation and status reading.
No timeline, team capacity, or browser/platform targets are given, so ordering here is dependency-based, not schedule-based.
The repair feedback did not specify failed_criteria or missing_evidence, so it is unclear what distinguished this candidate from the rejected one beyond re-issuing it.
